pattern.crimePattern: elderly musician kills the band manager who was replacing the live band with a DJ
pattern.notes: Fictional band, families and DJ. Taarab is a living tradition; the case depicts one fictional man's act, never the music or its community. Tone: quiet, sad, respectful.

ob.reportedBy: The father of the bride, wedding hall, Majengo
ob.text: The father of a bride reports that Amina Shee (45), manager of the taarab band Nyota ya Pwani, was found dead in the store room behind the stage of a community hall in Majengo during the wedding, at 23:40.

people.name: Amina Shee
people.occupation: Manager and booker, Nyota ya Pwani
people.bio: Has booked the band's weddings for fifteen years. Collects the fees and pays the musicians.

image.brief: Swahili Kenyan woman, mid 40s, an elegant embroidered dera and a silk headscarf, a cash envelope and a phone in her hands, warm and businesslike, ID-photo framing

people.name: Mzee Abdulrahman Kibwana
people.occupation: Oud player, Nyota ya Pwani, for 52 years
people.bio: A legend of Mombasa taarab. Gentle, everyone's grandfather. His small share of each wedding fee is his only income.

image.brief: Swahili Kenyan elder, mid 70s, a white kanzu and embroidered kofia, thin silver beard, an oud resting against his shoulder, long fingers, a gentle tired face, ID-photo framing

people.name: Mohamed "DJ Moha" Bwana
people.bio: Fought publicly with the band over who would play tonight's wedding.

image.brief: Swahili Kenyan man, early 30s, designer-style sunglasses at night, a bomber jacket, headphones round his neck, a confident grin, ID-photo framing

people.name: Mwanaisha Fadhili
people.bio: Has sung with the band for thirty years. Wanted to take over as manager.

image.brief: Swahili Kenyan woman, mid 50s, a shimmering gold dera, heavy kohl, a microphone in her hand, a voice you can see in her face, ID-photo framing

people.name: Twaha Kibwana
people.bio: Plays keyboard beside his grandfather. Says Babu never left the stage.

people.name: Bi Zainab Said
people.bio: Booked the band for her daughter's wedding, as her mother booked it for hers.

places.name: Curtain and passage behind the stage

locations.name: Community hall, Majengo
locations.description: A wedding night. The hall is hung with lights; women on one side, men on the other, the bride on a decorated stage. The band plays on a low platform: oud, violin, keyboard, drum. Behind the band, a curtain, a passage, and a store room where the caterers keep their trays.

hotspots.label: Store room
hotspots.text: Amina lies beside a heavy brass tray stand. The night's cash envelope is still in her hand.

hotspots.label: Under the stand
hotspots.text: Something light and pale under the stand: a broken quill.

hotspots.label: Her phone
hotspots.text: Her phone on a crate. Her son arrives with the code.

hotspots.label: Her bag
hotspots.text: Her handbag, a folded contract inside.

hotspots.label: The stage
hotspots.text: The oud lies across the old man's chair. The keyboard's sampler pads glow faintly.

hotspots.label: Mother of the bride
hotspots.text: Bi Zainab stands between the two sides of the hall, holding her daughter's veil.

facts.text: Amina Shee, manager of the taarab band Nyota ya Pwani, was found dead in the store room behind the stage at 23:40.
Amina was struck with a heavy brass tray stand.
The night's cash is still in its envelope in her hand.
Under the stand: a broken feather plectrum (risha), the old kind cut from an eagle's quill.
Mwanaisha: "Only the Mzee uses a feather risha. Everyone else uses plastic. He cuts his own."
Amina's WhatsApp to DJ Moha, 21:50: 'Baada ya leo, wazee wamekwisha. Contract yako inaanza tarehe moja Oktoba.' (After today the old men are finished. Your contract starts on 1 October.)
Amina's PesaPap, 23:05: KSh 6,000 to ABDULRAHMAN KIBWANA, reference 'last fee, asante'.
Signed agreement with DJ Moha: "modern taarab package", all bookings from 1 October.
Wedding video, 23:08–23:24: from 23:12 to 23:19 the oud player's chair is empty, but the oud is still heard. Twaha's left hand is on the keyboard's sampler pads.
Video: at 23:12 the Mzee stands, leans his oud on his chair and goes through the curtain behind the stage, towards the store room. At 23:19 he comes back through it.
Video: Mwanaisha sings centre stage from 23:08 to 23:24.
Video: Twaha's hands are on the keyboard throughout.
Video: Bi Zainab sits with the bride on the women's side throughout.
DJ Moha's public live stream: setting up his sound system in the car park from 23:00 to 23:30, his face on camera throughout.
Bi Zainab: the Kibwanas and the Shees are related by marriage and have played every family wedding for decades. "There is no feud. There is only love."
Twaha: "Babu was on stage beside me the whole second set. I can see him from my keyboard."
Twaha admits that for a year he has played his grandfather's oud parts from a recording when Babu's hands tire. Tonight Babu went out "for a few minutes".
Mzee Kibwana: "Amina is my daughter's friend. I held her at her naming ceremony."
DJ Moha: "I was setting up outside. I was live the whole time."
DJ Moha: "Those two families have always fought. Ask anyone."
Mwanaisha: "I sang the whole set."
Mwanaisha admits she wanted to take over as the band's manager. "I wanted to save us. Not like this."

interrogations.intro: Twaha sits on the edge of the stage with his hands between his knees. "Babu was beside me. The whole time. I can see him from my keyboard."

topics.reply: Auntie Amina booked every wedding we ever played. She was family.

interrogations.intro: The Mzee sits with his oud across his knees, very straight. He greets Amani in the old way, with both hands.

topics.reply: A long silence. Then: "Fifty-two years." Nothing more.
She paid me. She always paid me. She said thank you.

interrogations.intro: DJ Moha leans on his speaker stack in the car park. "Don't look at me. I wasn't even inside."

topics.reply: The old men are finished, that's just business. Those two families have always fought anyway. Ask anyone.

interrogations.intro: Mwanaisha still has the microphone in her hand. She doesn't seem to know it. "I sang. I sang the whole time."

topics.reply: Only the Mzee uses a feather risha. Everyone else uses plastic. He cuts his own.
I wanted to be manager. I wanted to save us. Not like this. Never like this.

interrogations.intro: Bi Zainab holds her daughter's veil in both hands. "My mother booked this band. I booked this band."

topics.reply: He played at my wedding. There is no feud between those families. There is only love.
My niece filmed the whole second set. Take it. Look at it.

contradictions.reaction: Babu's hands get tired. For a year I have played his oud parts from a recording so he can rest. Nobody is supposed to know. Tonight he went out for a few minutes. That's all. That's all it was.

words.text: she was ending the band he'd played in for fifty years
a feud between the two families

prosecutor.pass: Fifty years of music, and seven minutes. I'll ask the court to remember both.
fail: Doesn't hold up. The DJ was live on camera in the car park. Watch the wedding video again: whose chair is empty?
No. Listen to the oud, then look at the chair.

prosecutor.pass: After today, the old men are finished. She wrote it herself.
fail: He did it. But she had paid him, at 23:05. That isn't why.
There is no feud. Read her message to the DJ.

proof.concludes: The video shows the oud player's chair empty from 23:12 to 23:19 while a recording plays, and the Mzee going through the curtain towards the store room. Twaha's lie covered for his grandfather's tired hands, and for his absence.
That evening Amina paid the Mzee his "last fee" and signed the band's bookings over to a DJ from 1 October.
The broken feather plectrum under the stand is the kind only the Mzee uses. Mzee Abdulrahman Kibwana killed her because she was ending the band.

eliminations.why: DJ Moha was live on camera in the car park from 23:00 to 23:30.
Twaha's hands are on the keyboard throughout the video.
Bi Zainab sat with the bride on the women's side throughout.
She paid him his fee at 23:05.
The families are related by marriage; there is no feud.
The cash is still in the envelope in her hand.
That is Mwanaisha's ambition, and Mwanaisha was singing.

reconstruction.text: Amina signs a "modern taarab package" with a DJ: playback tracks and two young singers, cheaper than a live band. After tonight, Nyota ya Pwani has no more bookings.
23:05. She sends the Mzee his last fee, with a thank-you.
23:12. Twaha starts the recorded oud on his sampler, as he has for a year whenever his grandfather's hands tire. The Mzee leans his oud on the chair and goes through the curtain.
In the store room he pleads once more. She says no, kindly. The brass stand. His risha snaps in his fingers.
23:19. He is back in his chair with the oud on his knee. The bride is still dancing.

tier1.line: Watch the second set. Listen to the oud, and look at who is playing it.

tier2.line: A feather plectrum under the stand. Ask the singer who still cuts his own.

tier1.line: Read what she sent the DJ at ten to ten.

tier2.line: After today, the old men are finished.

glossary.def: Sung coastal poetry with an orchestra; Mombasa's wedding music.
Plectrum for the oud; traditionally cut from a feather quill.
Respectful word for an older man.
Respectful title for a woman, like "Mrs".
Long white robe worn by men.
Embroidered cap, often worn by Muslim men.
A long, loose, light dress worn on the coast.
Fictional mobile-money service used in the game.

ui.beatNotes: Video as evidence: scrubbed frame by frame with its timestamp. The audio waveform beside it shows the oud continuing while the chair is empty: picture and sound disagree, and that disagreement is the clue.
